risk_reasons: Calls the Stripe billing API destructively during the account-offboarding purge, which is itself irreversible.
Runs inside worker/ job handlers on the single-replica Railway worker.
Changes Stripe webhook ingress control flow, deciding whether Stripe retries an event or stops.
Changes an owner-facing deletion receipt and the published privacy policy, both compliance disclosures.
goal: A delete_data account purge clears the identifying fields on its Stripe Customer before the tombstone, discloses what survives at Stripe in the deletion receipt and the privacy policy, and stops a no-account Stripe subscription event from throwing once it is older than fifteen minutes.
non_goals: Deleting the Stripe Customer. Deletion detaches invoices and cannot be undone.
Altering, voiding, or redacting already-finalized Stripe invoices, charges, or PaymentIntents.
Removing Stripe Tax identifiers. tax_ids are separate objects the Customer update cannot reach.
Redacting the Stripe Customer for cancel_only offboarding. Only delete_data reaches the purge worker.
Adding a database migration or any schema change. db_touching is true only because the change edits two live-DB integration suites, so the gate must provision the test database and run them.
Making the event-age argument optional. It is required, so the compiler proves every call site supplies it.

A deferred-reconciliation outbox topic and worker for an acked stale subscription event. Owner decision 2026-09-03 after plan rounds 1 and 2: checkout-completed already reads provider-current state and rolls back on canceled, so the end state is correct, and today's code reaches it after three days of retries plus an alert storm. The row is recorded with the reclaimable stale_ignored status, NOT processed, so an operator resending the event from Stripe still reprocesses it. Round 2 proved that acking with processed would have made recovery strictly worse than today.
Changing the 7-day STALE_EVENT_THRESHOLD_SECONDS anomaly guard in worker/ingress/stripe.ts.
Restructuring the privacy policy into a new retention section.
Counting retained Stripe invoices in the receipt.
user_visible_behavior: The purge receipt email gains one sentence: RepWorth cleared the identifying details from its payment processor's customer record, and paid invoices with their billing name and address are retained for tax and accounting purposes.
The privacy policy deletion paragraph names what survives at the payment processor after deletion.

Operational: a customer.subscription.updated or customer.subscription.deleted event whose customer has no account, and whose event.created is older than 15 minutes, is logged and acked with HTTP 200 instead of 500. The inbound_events row records stale_ignored, not failed, so HealthAlertPoller stops raising inbound_events_failed for that class. stale_ignored stays reclaimable by claimInboundEvent, so an operator resending the event from Stripe still reprocesses it.

Operational: after a delete_data purge, the Stripe Customer in the dashboard shows no name, email, phone, description, address, or shipping, and carries exactly one metadata key naming the offboarding id.
invariants: The Stripe Customer is never deleted. Only stripe.customers.update is called.

Redaction runs strictly before runParentTombstonePurgeStage (worker/jobs/account-offboarding/purge-stages.ts:685) and therefore before finalizePurgeInTransaction nulls account_offboardings.stripe_customer_id at line 935.
A stripe_customer_id still referenced by any other account row that is not itself purged is never redacted. The stage skips and records the reason.
The stage is idempotent. A re-run after a partial purge attempt reaches the same end state and raises no error.
A null row.stripe_customer_id makes the stage a no-op, not a failure.
Retryable Stripe errors throw so BullMQ retries and the purge does not finalize. A permanent resource_missing counts as success because the identifiers are already gone.
The receipt never names a retained identifier, an invoice number, or a Stripe id. It names categories only, matching the existing retained-suppression sentence.

TABLE_DISPOSITIONS stays exactly equal to the real tenant-table set. The Stripe Customer classification lives in a separate export and never enters ACCOUNT_OFFBOARDING_TABLES or PURGE_VERIFICATION_TABLES.
verificationQuery keeps its fail-closed default. No new table name reaches it without SQL.
The 15-minute bound is read from the Stripe event's created timestamp, never from the Subscription object's own created field.
Under 15 minutes the two handlers still throw AccountNotProvisionedYetError, preserving the out-of-order retry that checkout-completed depends on.
The redaction stage writes no raw owner identifier to logs or provider_dispositions. The stripe customer id is scrubbed the same way provider-disposition.ts scrubs a resource reference.

The shared-customer guard and every non-null binding assignment to accounts.stripe_customer_id hold the same customer-keyed advisory lock, so the guard's count cannot go stale between the read and the Stripe call. The lock is taken in applyStripeSubscriptionStateInternal, which both exported entry points funnel through. Note that line 741 of purge-stages.ts also writes the column, to NULL; only non-null bindings are in scope.

Lock order is fixed: writers take the account-scoped tier entitlement lock first and the customer-keyed binding lock second. The redaction stage takes only the binding lock and requests no other, so no cycle exists.

createCheckoutSession passes customer_email and never customer, so Stripe mints a new Customer per session and no code path binds an existing Customer to a second account. This is the premise the D8 residual rests on and it is pinned by a test, not assumed.
A stale no-account subscription event stays reclaimable. It is recorded with a status that claimInboundEvent will reclaim, so an operator resending the event from Stripe still reprocesses it.
No test in this feature is written as todo or skipped. A pending test cannot make vitest fail, so it is not a promise.
Stripe teardown has already cancelled the subscription before purge runs, so clearing address cannot break an active automatic_tax calculation.
edge_cases: Shared Stripe Customer: two accounts hold the same stripe_customer_id and only one is purged. The stage counts other accounts inside its transaction, skips the Stripe call, and appends a system provider-redaction record naming skipped_shared_customer. The purge still finalizes.
Customer already deleted at Stripe: the retrieve returns a deleted customer or raises resource_missing. Treated as success.
Customer already redacted by an earlier attempt: the retrieve shows the fields empty and the offboarding metadata key present. The stage makes no write and returns already_redacted.

Metadata merge semantics: stripe.customers.update MERGES metadata, so a single call with only the offboarding key leaves old keys. The stage retrieves first and sets every existing key to the empty string in the same write.
row.stripe_customer_id is null: not applicable, no Stripe call, stage returns not_applicable.
Stripe rate limit or connection error: classified retryable, throws, PurgeWorker calls markPurgeRetryableFailure and BullMQ retries.

Terminal BullMQ attempt with a still-failing Stripe call: markPurgeTerminalFailure runs and the offboarding lands failed. The receipt is never sent, so it never claims a redaction that did not happen.
A no-account subscription event exactly at the 15-minute boundary: the bound is strict, so an age strictly greater than 900 seconds acks and 900 or less throws.
Clock skew makes event.created appear in the future: the computed age is negative, which is under the bound, so the handler throws and Stripe retries. Fail toward the existing behavior.
The acked-old branch still raises one Sentry warning so the case stays visible without paging.

rollback_plan: Revert the merge commit. No migration and no schema change, so no data rollback is required. A Stripe Customer already redacted stays redacted; that is irreversible by design and is the intended erasure. Reverting restores the previous webhook behavior, which throws for every no-account subscription event, and restores the previous receipt and policy text.
observability: A structured worker log line per redaction outcome: redacted, already_redacted, skipped_shared_customer, not_applicable, customer_absent. The stripe customer id is scrubbed.
The existing Sentry account_offboarding_purge_failed alert covers a redaction failure, tagged step purge.
The system provider-redaction record on account_offboardings.provider_dispositions is the durable per-account record of what happened at Stripe.
A new Sentry warning when a no-account subscription event is acked for age, so the case stays visible after HealthAlertPoller stops counting it.
HealthAlertPoller's inbound_events_failed:stripe:customer.subscription.* rate is the success signal: it should fall to zero for the no-account class.
